evidence_text: IFRS explicitly prohibits the use of the LIFO method, which is permitted under US GAAP (ASC 330) and commonly used to provide tax savings during inflationary periods by reporting lower profits. The LIFO method can provide tax savings during periods of inflation since it results in lower reported profits.
mechanism: Using LIFO during inflation increases the cost of goods sold, reducing taxable income and thus providing tax savings.

evidence_text: IFRS adopts the FIFO method [IAS 2.25]. The divergence in inventory valuation between IFRS and US GAAP represents a significant accounting difference, primarily involving the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) and Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) models.
mechanism: The adoption of FIFO under IFRS and LIFO under US GAAP creates a difference in inventory valuation.

evidence_text: GAAP (ASC 330) utilizes the LIFO method. The divergence in inventory valuation between IFRS and US GAAP represents a significant accounting difference, primarily involving the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) and Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) models.
mechanism: The adoption of LIFO under US GAAP and FIFO under IFRS creates a difference in inventory valuation.

evidence_text: IFRS requires inventory to be measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value (NRV). US GAAP (ASC 330) distinguishes between the "lower of cost or market" for LIFO users and "lower of cost or NRV" for FIFO users.
IFRS allows the reversal of previous inventory write-downs if the value subsequently recovers. US GAAP prohibits such reversals once the inventory has been written down to a new cost basis.
